questions.question: What identifies the intended server application endpoint in an initial TCP segment?
questions.explanation: The server listens at the destination transport port.

option_explanations.A: TTL limits the life of the encapsulating IP packet.
option_explanations.B: The receive window advertises buffer space.
option_explanations.C: The server listens at the destination transport port.
option_explanations.D: A source MAC identifies a link-layer sender.

questions.question: Which exchange normally establishes a TCP connection?
questions.explanation: Both peers synchronize initial sequence numbers and acknowledge the other peer's SYN.

option_explanations.A: The opening exchange starts with SYN and does not use FIN.
option_explanations.B: FIN closes a stream rather than establishing it.
option_explanations.C: Both peers synchronize initial sequence numbers and acknowledge the other peer's SYN.
option_explanations.D: RST resets a connection attempt instead of opening one.

questions.question: Which field exists in the UDP header?
questions.explanation: UDP carries source port, destination port, length and checksum fields.

option_explanations.A: UDP has no advertised receive window.
option_explanations.D: UDP carries source port, destination port, length and checksum fields.

questions.question: Two TCP connections share a server address and destination port. How can the server distinguish them?

options.A: Their source addresses or source ports differ
options.B: They must have different destination MACs
options.C: Each connection uses a different IP protocol number
options.D: Each connection requires a different TTL

questions.explanation: The two endpoint addresses and ports identify a TCP connection.

option_explanations.A: The two endpoint addresses and ports identify a TCP connection.
option_explanations.B: The same server or next-hop MAC can carry both connections.
option_explanations.C: Both use the same IP protocol number for TCP.
option_explanations.D: TTL is a hop limit rather than a connection identifier.

questions.question: What does a cumulative TCP ACK of 520 indicate for ordinary byte transfer?

options.A: Bytes through 519 have been received in order
options.B: The server listened on TCP port 520
options.C: Byte 520 is the last byte received in order

questions.explanation: The acknowledgment number is the next byte position expected.

option_explanations.A: The acknowledgment number is the next byte position expected.
option_explanations.B: The ACK field does not encode a port.
option_explanations.C: 520 is the next expected byte, not the last one received.
option_explanations.D: The advertised window has its own header field.

questions.question: A TCP segment is lost and its retransmission timer expires. What does the sending TCP normally do?

options.C: Discards all previously acknowledged bytes at the receiver

questions.explanation: TCP uses retransmission to recover missing data.

option_explanations.A: TCP uses retransmission to recover missing data.
option_explanations.B: A TCP retransmission does not change the connection's transport.
option_explanations.C: The receiver retains already acknowledged bytes.
option_explanations.D: The destination port identifies the existing connection and stays the same.

questions.question: Which TCP header field advertises how much receive space the peer should account for when sending?
questions.explanation: The advertised window limits how much additional sequence space the sender may use.

option_explanations.A: A source port identifies a sending endpoint.
option_explanations.B: The urgent pointer relates to urgent data.
option_explanations.C: The advertised window limits how much additional sequence space the sender may use.
option_explanations.D: Data Offset gives the header length.

questions.question: A TCP segment beginning at sequence 700 carries 40 bytes in order with no SYN or FIN. What cumulative ACK is expected if no later data has arrived?
questions.explanation: The data occupy sequence numbers 700 through 739, so the next expected byte is 740.

option_explanations.A: 739 is the last received byte, not the next expected byte.
option_explanations.B: 700 is the first byte of the received segment.
option_explanations.C: 741 would require one more byte or a sequence-consuming flag.
option_explanations.D: The data occupy sequence numbers 700 through 739, so the next expected byte is 740.

questions.question: A receiver temporarily advertises a zero window. What is the immediate implication for ordinary new data?

options.A: The sender switches the connection to UDP
options.B: The receiver must send a reset
options.C: The sender pauses new data until the window opens
options.D: The sender sends another full receive buffer

questions.explanation: Zero receive space stops ordinary new data. TCP uses window probes so the sender can detect reopening.

option_explanations.A: A zero window does not alter the transport protocol.
option_explanations.B: A reset would terminate the connection, which an advertised zero window does not require.
option_explanations.C: Zero receive space stops ordinary new data. TCP uses window probes so the sender can detect reopening.
option_explanations.D: Sending another block of ordinary data would ignore the advertised limit.

questions.question: What does TCP Data Offset specify?

options.A: The TCP header length in 32-bit words
options.C: The sequence number of the first unacknowledged byte
options.D: The IPv4 header length in octets

questions.explanation: Data Offset tells a receiver where the TCP payload begins, including space for TCP options.

option_explanations.A: Data Offset tells a receiver where the TCP payload begins, including space for TCP options.
option_explanations.B: The advertised Window field indicates receive space.
option_explanations.C: Sequence and acknowledgment numbers track positions in the byte stream.
option_explanations.D: IPv4 uses IHL for its own header length.
